verdict.root_cause: Not established. The only confirmed fault is a caller-visible error regression at frontend: error ratio rose from ~0.017% baseline to ~2.3% mean with peaks near 11.5%, and its single change point sits at 13:41:30 — about 21 minutes before the 14:03 cartservice alert [tr_dd2ff7204302]. The pattern is bursty and partial (minimum still zero, sd above mean), consistent with a fraction of requests failing rather than any dependency being hard down [tr_dd2ff7204302]. Nothing implicates cartservice: its logs show dense, error-free cart operations at both window edges through 14:05:09, with no restart or Redis-failure lines [tr_a4e370be1a5a], and its automated apply-then-revert change cycle (hotfix image, egress-delay sidecar, REDIS_ADDR on a non-default port) had its last apply reverted ~1.3h before onset, roughly an hour before the frontend change point [tr_a2db3adb0a37]. cartservice's own error/latency/saturation telemetry is unmeasurable — the queried series is empty in both windows, including the denominator, so the labels do not match what it exports [tr_9c4e7f094d00]. The erroring hop is unidentified and four graph edges went unmeasured.
verdict.reasoning: I name frontend only because it is the one service with a demonstrated, quantified regression [tr_dd2ff7204302] — a statement about where failure is observable, not about where it originates. Three of four dispatches went to cartservice and all came back exculpatory or empty: healthy continuous logging at both edges [tr_a4e370be1a5a], no samples at all for error, latency or saturation [tr_9c4e7f094d00], and every suspicious change reverted before onset [tr_a2db3adb0a37]. The frontend change point at 13:41:30 falls about an hour after that final revert and 21 minutes before the alert timestamp the investigation anchored on, so the fault aligns with neither the change stream nor 14:03. With no per-dependency dimension on the frontend query and no latency or rate series returned, the failing call path cannot be attributed. Choosing bad_config or dependency_latency would mean classifying by the act visible in the change log rather than by an observed mechanism, and that log says the act had already ended.
open_questions: Which frontend dependency carries the erroring calls — the error ratio was queried unfiltered, with no per-dependency or per-route breakdown [tr_dd2ff7204302].
What happened to cartservice between 13:33:10 and 14:04:54; that interval, containing both 14:03 and the 13:41:30 change point, was truncated out of the log result [tr_a4e370be1a5a].
checkoutservice alerted at 14:03:30 and was never dispatched to; its errors, latency and dependency edges are wholly unmeasured, as are the four edges triage flagged.

alternatives.root_cause: A residual effect of the reverted cartservice changes (injected egress delay or the non-default-port REDIS_ADDR override) continued to degrade cart calls after the recorded revert.
alternatives.why_not: Both changes were reverted ~1.3-1.6h before onset and about an hour before the frontend change point, and cartservice logs show no errors or connection failures at either window edge [tr_a2db3adb0a37, tr_a4e370be1a5a]; a revert cannot be re-applied as a fix.

alternatives.root_cause: An unexamined downstream service on the frontend request path began erroring intermittently around 13:41:30, with cartservice and checkoutservice alerts being propagation rather than origin.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and consistent with the bursty partial-failure shape, but no dispatch measured any service other than frontend and cartservice, so it names no mechanism and no actionable target [tr_dd2ff7204302].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected or claimed. The only confirmed observable is frontend's error ratio at ~2.3% mean (peaks ~11.5%) against a ~0.017% baseline with a change point at 13:41:30 [tr_dd2ff7204302]; nothing in the permitted action set has been shown to move it. The next useful step is measurement, not remediation: a per-dependency/per-route breakdown of frontend's calls_total error ratio to identify which of adservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, checkoutservice or cartservice carries the erroring calls, an untruncated cart-service log read over 13:33:10-14:04:54, and any telemetry at all for checkoutservice, which alerted at 14:03:30 and was never dispatched to.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention would be wrong if a per-dependency error breakdown, or the unexamined 13:33:10-14:04:54 cart-service log interval, named a specific service and mechanism that one of the permitted actions addresses. Concretely: if the truncated log interval turned out to contain a restart or Redis-connection-failure banner, restart_service on cartservice would become arguable; if change history showed an apply still outstanding at 13:41:30, rollback_image or revert_config would become arguable. Neither holds on current evidence. Note also that the leading remediation candidate, cartservice, cannot be verified after any action: its error/latency/saturation series are empty in both incident and baseline windows including the denominator [tr_9c4e7f094d00], so an effect on cartservice is not observable in this system's metrics and could only be inferred indirectly from frontend's aggregate ratio - which is itself unattributed. Acting on an unobservable target is not a prediction.
proposal.risk: The risk here is the risk of acting, which is why I am not. Every permitted action fails its own preconditions. rollback_image and revert_config both require the evidence to name a deploy or config change inside the incident window; the most recent cartservice change is a revert ~1.3h before onset, roughly an hour before the frontend change point, with no apply-type change left outstanding [tr_a2db3adb0a37] - so a rollback would move cartservice off a configuration that evidence explicitly rules out as active, plausibly re-applying the hotfix image or the non-default REDIS_ADDR port that the automation had already withdrawn, and manufacturing a real cart outage on top of an unexplained one. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state; cart-service logs show dense, error-free operation at both window edges through 14:05:09 with no restart or startup banners [tr_a4e370be1a5a], so a restart would discard a warm cache and reset connections on a process shown to be healthy. It would also destroy the in-window state needed to diagnose the real fault. scale_service is unavailable by ADR-0029.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody, by design - no change is made, so no caller sees a reset. The cost of abstaining is carried by the ongoing frontend error regression, which continues at ~2.3% of requests with bursts to ~11.5% [tr_dd2ff7204302] and is visible to loadgenerator and to end users until someone identifies the erroring hop. Had I proposed against cartservice, its inbound callers - frontend and checkoutservice - would have seen connection resets during the container recreate, and checkoutservice is itself an unmeasured alerting service, so that disturbance would have been indistinguishable from the fault under investigation.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerted within 30 seconds spanning cart, frontend and checkout — that is a multi-service pattern I cannot dismiss as a single quiet warning. Cartservice alerting first with fanout to its consumers suggests a shared downstream dependency, but the class is a weak prior only.
